content: Phenobarbital interacts with various drugs by influencing their metabolism, primarily through hepatic and intestinal enzymes such as CYP3A4, CYP1A2, CYP2C19, and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. These interactions can lead to either decreased drug levels or effects, or increased sedation and toxicity. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Tolvalptan: Phenobarbital reduces its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 2. Tovorafenib: Phenobarbital decreases its levels by increasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Trabectedin: Phenobarbital reduces its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Tucatinib: Phenobarbital decreases its levels through CYP3A4 metabolism and other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Ubrogepant: Phenobarbital lowers its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Ulipristal: Phenobarbital reduces its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Upadacitinib: Phenobarbital decreases its levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 8. Abiraterone: Phenobarbital reduces its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 9. Acebutolol: Phenobarbital decreases its levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and consider a higher beta-blocker dose. 10. Amitriptyline: Phenobarbital reduces its levels via CYP2C19, CYP3A4, and P-glycoprotein metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Amlodipine: Phenobarbital decreases its levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Amiodarone: Phenobarbital reduces its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Aripiprazole: Phenobarbital decreases its levels through CYP3A4 metabolism and increases sedation. Use caution and monitor. 14. Atorvastatin: Phenobarbital lowers its levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Phenobarbital reduces their levels through CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein metabolism, increasing the risk of endometrial hyperplasia. Use caution and monitor. 16. Buprenorphine: Phenobarbital decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and increases sedation. Monitor closely, especially with subdermal implants or long-acting injections. 17. Bupropion: Phenobarbital reduces its levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 18. Carvedilol: Phenobarbital decreases its levels through CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose. 19. Citalopram: Phenobarbital reduces its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Clonazepam: Phenobarbital decreases its levels through CYP3A4 metabolism and increases sedation. Use caution and monitor. 21. Clozapine: Phenobarbital reduces its levels via CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism and increases sedation. Use caution and monitor. 22. Codeine: Phenobarbital increases sedation when coadministered. Use caution and monitor. 23. Colchicine: Phenobarbital decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 24. Conjugated Estrogens: Phenobarbital reduces their levels through CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Cortisone: Phenobarbital decreases its levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Crizotinib: Phenobarbital reduces its levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
